_doc: Every numeric parameter and rule the pipeline uses. Read by pipeline/common.py. The text (words, section marks, verse numbers) is Miqra according to the Masorah via ../mam.py. See HANDOFF.md section 2 for the meaning of each entry (written for the earlier Leningrad build; the costs and rules are unchanged).

cost_function._doc: cost(reading) = alpha * ((W - T) / S)^2 + break_cost(last verse of the reading). W = words in the reading, T = its target, S = normaliser. The plan minimises the sum over all readings (exact dynamic programming).

torah_break_costs._doc: Cost of ending a reading after a given Torah verse. First matching rule wins, in this order: book_end, petuha, setuma, aliyah_end, chapter_end, otherwise 'verse'. Then hand scene breaks (config/hand_breaks.json) lower the cost to 'scene' when the current cost is higher than 'scene'.

nakh_break_costs._doc: Cost of ending a reading after a given Neviʾim/Ketuvim verse. First matching rule wins: book_end, petuha, setuma, psalm_end (chapter end in Ps), chapter_end, ps119_stanza (Ps 119, verse number divisible by stanza size), otherwise 'verse'. Then: if the verse is a hand scene break and cost > scene, cost = scene; else if cost == verse and the book is poetic, cost = verse_poetic.

plans._doc: Two reading schemes x two week lengths. Keys '6' and '5' are days of reading per week; the remaining day(s) are catch-up days and carry no reading.

continuous._doc: Plan 1 (Even Tanakh Year). Torah read straight through in readings = weeks * days_per_week, ignoring parasha boundaries. T = S = total Torah words / readings for every reading.

parasha._doc: Plan 2 (Tanakh by the Parasha). Each of the 54 parashiyyot is split on its own into exactly days_per_week readings, so readings = 54 * days_per_week. Within a parasha, T = S = parasha words / days_per_week. No maximum reading length. A reading can never cross a parasha (and so never a book).

nakh._doc: Used by both plans. Neviʾim and Ketuvim are two separate continuous streams, each split into exactly as many readings as the Torah track has. Day target: Ttot = (Torah words + Neviʾim words + Ketuvim words) / readings; remainder_d = Ttot - torah_words_d; target_track_d = remainder_d * W_track / (W_neviim + W_ketuvim). S = mean of that track's targets. Readings may cross book boundaries (this is how short books end up read together). Each reading has at least 1 verse.
